Syed Ziaul Karim with Khurshid Alam Khan, Advocates—For the Petitioners
Sharifuddin Chaklader, Advocate—For the Opposite Parties Nos. 1-5 with the leave of the Court.
parties:
Amirunnessa and others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Abdul Mannan Howlader and others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment: The lower appellate Court being the final court of fact failed to apply his judicial mind in not considering that the plaintiff's proved the execution of the unregistered deed of gift Ext. 1 dated 27.7.64 by examining the scribe and other disinterested witnesses who were present at the time of execution of the said basic document of title in favour of the donee plaintiffs. It is true that said deed of gift dated 27.7.64 Ext. 1 has not been registered but the fact remains that as to the delivery of possession by the donor in favour of the donee plaintiffs, has been well established by evidence on record and both the courts below had found possession in their favour. I therefore, hold that the plaintiffs, being in exclusive possession over the statutory period of limitation from the date of institution of the suit by the plaintiffs in the year 1984 and to the complete ouster of the defendants for about 20 years from the suit property, have acquired a valid title even on the basis of the defective deed of gift being an unregistered one. It further appears that the defendant could neither challenge the said unregistered deed Ext. 1 nor file any suit to establish their alleged right in the suit property within the statutory period of 12 years and it is further held that the defect of the plaintiffs deed of gift has been cured with the passage of time and the plaintiffs' imperfect title has been perfected by the said period. This legal aspect having not been considered by the lower appellate Court he committed error of law in arriving at the finding as stated above and this has resulted in an error in the decision causing failure of justice. It further appears that the trial Court while disposing of the suit framed as many as 8 (eight) issues but the learned lower appellate Court, being the final court of fact failed to come to his own independent findings on those issues and thereby committed error of law in not following the mandatory provision of Order 41 rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
